readings.title: A uniform for another season
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A hotel replaced its staff uniforms every spring, even when many garments were still usable. Its laundry manager suggested keeping jackets and replacing only badly worn shirts. A small trial showed that a consistent appearance did not require every item to be new. The hotel then hired a local tailor to adjust jackets for incoming employees. Some sizes could not be altered successfully, so those garments were kept for future staff rather than forced into poor fits. Spending fell, and employees reported greater comfort. The change depended on flexible purchasing and careful fitting, not simply a request to buy less.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The mysterious fibre mixture
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At a textile workshop, visitors tried to identify fabrics by touch. Several confidently described a soft cloth as cotton, although its label showed a mixture of three fibres. The instructor explained that finishing processes could change how a fabric felt. She then asked participants to compare labels, expected use and care requirements. A strong outdoor cover and a light summer shirt had different needs, so there was no single best fibre for every product. Visitors left with a more useful habit: asking what evidence supported a claim instead of relying entirely on how a material looked or felt.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: When a repair class changed direction
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An evening sewing class initially planned to teach decorative stitches. On the first night, learners brought trousers with loose hems, bags with broken straps and shirts missing buttons. The tutor realised that practical repairs mattered more to this group than decoration. She reorganised lessons around the items people had brought, while still introducing the same basic hand movements. Attendance rose because learners could see immediate results. Decorative work returned later as an optional project. The tutor did not abandon her expertise; she found a different route into it by listening to the purposes that learners brought to class.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The swap that needed a mirror
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A neighbourhood clothing swap attracted many visitors, but a large number left without taking anything. Organisers first assumed the selection was too small. Conversations revealed another reason: people could not judge fit, because the hall had neither a mirror nor a private changing area. At the next event, organisers borrowed folding screens and placed a full-length mirror nearby. They also labelled sizes as approximate because older clothes sometimes stretched or shrank. More items found new users, although the number donated was similar. Improving the conditions for making a choice proved more useful than merely collecting additional stock.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into Chinese.

The value of a garment does not disappear when a small part wears out. A replaced button or repaired pocket may allow it to serve for another year. Yet repair becomes less likely when people cannot find spare parts or clear instructions. Designing products for continued use therefore involves the services around them as well as the materials inside them.
translation.referenceAnswer: 一件衣服不会因为某个小部位磨损就失去价值。更换纽扣或修补口袋，可能使它再用一年。然而，如果人们找不到零配件或清楚的说明，就更不可能进行修补。因此，为持续使用而设计产品，既涉及产品本身的材料，也涉及配套服务。
translation.explanation: 参考译文展示一种可接受的表达；保留原文信息及逻辑、中文通顺的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 English words for this original simulation task.

Write a suggestion to a clothing shop asking it to offer a small repair service. Explain which repairs to include, how customers would benefit and how the shop could manage demand.
writing.sampleAnswer: I suggest that our local clothing shop offer a basic repair service one afternoon each week. Replacing buttons, repairing loose seams and shortening simple hems would be useful starting points. These small jobs could help customers continue wearing garments that already fit them well. The shop could publish clear prices and ask customers to book a short assessment before leaving an item. A tailor should explain when a repair is unsuitable or would cost more than expected. Limiting the first month's appointments would prevent long delays while staff learn how much work they can handle. Customers would gain convenient help, and the shop would build relationships based on care that continues after a purchase.
writing.explanation: 范文用于作答后参考；观点与例子可以不同，但须回应全部要求并表达清楚。
